content: 1. Hyperglycemia can occur due to insulin resistance associated with the use of protease inhibitors. Darunavir reduces the efficacy of exenatide injectable suspension through mechanisms involving other pathways. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports indicate hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. 2. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Similarly, fedratinib increases the levels or effects of cobicistat via the same mechanism. Dose adjustments for drugs metabolized by CYP3A4 may be necessary. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of felodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases the levels or effects of felodipine through the same pathway. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fentanyl by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inhibitors with fentanyl necessitates frequent monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation, with dose adjustments until stable effects are achieved. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fentanyl intranasal and transdermal formulations by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Frequent monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation is necessary when co-administering CYP3A4 inhibitors with fentanyl. 6. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of flecainide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administering with antiarrhythmics. Cobicistat also increases flecainide levels via the same mechanism. 7. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while fludrocortisone decreases darunavir levels through the same pathway. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of flunisolide (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine through other mechanisms. Darunavir also increases fluoxetine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose. Monitor antidepressant response. 11. Darunavir increases the levels of flurazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Alternatives should be considered if available. Cobicistat also increases flurazepam levels via the same mechanism. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels of fluticasone furoate (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir similarly increases fluticasone levels. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may significantly increase systemic exposure to fluticasone. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases fluvastatin levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with darunavir, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 14. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of cobicistat through other mechanisms. Careful dose titration of antidepressants is necessary when co-administered with SSRIs and cobicistat. Fluvoxamine also increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both darunavir and fosamprenavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (the major active metabolite of fostamatinib). Monitor for toxicities that may necessitate dose reduction. 17. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 19. Garlic decreases darunavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of gefitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Cobicistat similarly increases gefitinib levels. Co-administration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Darunavir decreases the effects of glimepiride through other mechanisms. Reports indicate hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Darunavir may increase or decrease glipizide levels. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. Alternatives should be considered if available. 24. Darunavir decreases the effects of glyburide through other mechanisms. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. 25. Grapefruit increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Green tea in combination with darunavir may increase the risk of bleeding. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Griseofulvin decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, the dosage should be reduced to half the recommended dose. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir similarly increases haloperidol levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Cobicistat similarly increases hydrocodone levels. 31. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while hydrocortisone decreases darunavir levels through the same pathway. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Cobicistat decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, reducing its efficacy. 33. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydroxprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Alternatives should be considered if available. Reduced formation of active metabolites may increase toxicity. 35. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone also increases darunavir levels. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect. Cobicistat similarly increases imipramine levels. 38. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir also increases darunavir levels. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 39. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin aspart through other mechanisms. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. 41. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin degludec by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. HIV protease inhibitors may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 42. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin detemir through other mechanisms. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. 43. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin glargine through other mechanisms. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. 44. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin glulisine through other mechanisms. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. 45. Darunavir decreases the effects of inhaled insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. HIV protease inhibitors may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 46. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin lispro through other mechanisms. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. 47. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin NPH through other mechanisms. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. 48. Darunavir decreases the effects of regular human insulin through other mechanisms. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. 49. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised.
